title: Primary Function
learningObjectives: Connect bushing function to an interference fit.
student: What is the mechanical function of the sleeve bushing after installation, and why is an interference fit useful for retaining it in the housing?
instructor: The bushing provides a replaceable bearing surface that supports and guides a mating shaft or pin. The interference fit develops retention after warm-up and helps prevent the bushing from moving relative to the housing.

title: Fit Condition at Room Temperature
student: Compare the bushing outside diameter with the housing bore diameter. Is the initial fit a clearance fit or an interference fit? Explain.
instructor: Because Db is greater than Dh, the room-temperature condition is an interference fit.

title: Installation Strategy
student: Why can cooling the bushing make installation easier without permanently changing its room-temperature dimensions?
instructor: Cooling produces reversible thermal contraction. The smaller temporary outside diameter permits insertion; after the bushing returns to room temperature, it expands toward its original dimensions and restores the interference fit.

title: Relevant Mechanical Response
student: Which bushing dimension controls installation, and in which direction must it change?
instructor: The bushing outside diameter controls insertion and must decrease through thermal contraction.

title: Relevant Parameters
student: Identify the geometric, thermal-property, and temperature inputs required to determine the cooled diameter and final temperature.
instructor: The required inputs are Db, Dh, c, Ti, and αb. Bushing bore, length, housing properties, and photographed-product dimensions are not needed.

title: Student-Generated Idealization
learningObjectives: Create a dimensional thermal model before viewing the reference.
student:
Draw simplified cross-sectional models of the bushing and housing bore at room temperature and after cooling. Label Db, Dh, c, Ti, ΔT, and Dcold.

Student idealization space
instructor: Show the room-temperature interference condition and the cooled bushing inside the unchanged housing bore with diametral clearance c. Apply ΔT only to the bushing.

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State assumptions supporting linear thermal deformation.
student: State the assumptions needed to use uniform linear thermal expansion/contraction for this installation.
instructor: Assume uniform bushing temperature, isotropic linear thermal expansion/contraction, constant αb, small thermal strain, an unchanged housing bore because the housing remains at Ti, no phase change or permanent deformation, and no evaluation of contact stresses after warm-up.

title: Mechanics Analysis Plan
student: Before substituting numbers, outline the sequence used to calculate interference, required cooled diameter, dimensional change, temperature change, and final temperature.

title: Room-Temperature Interference
student: Calculate δ = Db - Dh. Can the specified clearance exist at room temperature?

title: Required Dimensional Change
learningObjectives: Calculate and interpret signed diameter change.

title: Sensitivity and Engineering Judgment
learningObjectives: Predict the effect of increased clearance.
student: If the required assembly clearance c is increased, does the required final bushing temperature become warmer or colder? Explain using the governing relations.

title: Engineering Assessment and Limitations
student: State whether the calculated cooling requirement is physically plausible for a controlled installation process, and identify at least two effects neglected by this model.
